Subject: Tuesday reading club — attendance update before the review

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to send you an update on the Tuesday reading club at Knocknacarra before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November. I was disappointed to hear in your email of 30 October that the club was to be paused from January, though I understand the concerns about attendance and the increase in insurance costs. There has been a real change in the past few weeks, and I hope you might reconsider the pause in light of it.

We had 14 children last Tuesday, 3 November. That is up from five most weeks in September and nine by the middle of October. Since we started in September 2025, we have kept the same Tuesday slot, 3.30 to 4.45, in the upstairs meeting room at the library. It has taken time to build, but it now feels as though the club is finding its feet. I came home last Tuesday absolutely delighted.

There has been lovely support locally, too. Declan Moran, who owns Salthill Book Nook, has donated 120 books, mostly for the six-to-nine age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. It gives the children much more choice, and there is great excitement around choosing what to read next.

The numbers matter, of course, but there are smaller things happening that I wish you could see. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. Another child, who would not open a book in September, asked last week whether he could take two home. After all my years teaching, those moments still mean a great deal to me. It would be a terrible pity to stop just as the children are beginning to make the club their own.

There is also something I need to tell you directly, because I would much rather you heard it from me. I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers’ market and got carried away telling her how well things were going. I said, “Come along any Tuesday.” She would now like to come on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer.

I was wrong not to check with you first, plain and simple. I know that photographs of the children require your sign-off and the parental consent forms. My invitation should not have been given before speaking to you, and I am sorry for putting you in that position.

I think the coverage could be wonderful for the club, but only if it is done properly. I am very happy to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you have decided whether it should go ahead. If you do approve it, I would also be happy to collect the consent forms myself, following whatever arrangements you set out. There should be no assumption that either the visit or any photographs have been approved.

For now, my main hope is that you will have the new attendance figures before the 18th and give the proposed pause another look. I know the insurance question remains, and I would welcome a chance to talk through what might be possible.

Thanks, Niamh, for considering it, and for all your work supporting us.

Warm wishes,
[Your name]
